title: Local and remaining ozone by warmth slopes differed in one of four US bird samples in 1995-2024
abstract: We separated an ozone by warmth product into local state-year deviations and remaining terms. We used 30,465 selected US bird surveys in four region and period samples from 1995 to 2024. Models controlled route-observer groups, state-year groups and survey conditions. All four corrected intervals for the local product included zero. The local-minus-remaining contrast was below zero only in the West in 2010-2024: -2.84 recorded species per 10 ppb and 2 C, with a four-test interval of -5.37 to -0.31. A stricter route-count rule gave the same broad result. This test rejects a common coefficient for the two product terms in that sample. It does not establish a causal effect or a regional difference. Few western state clusters, selected routes, coarse exposures and detection bias limit inference. This is an exploratory diagnostic on reused records. Code, the input panel, source hashes, aggregate results and independent numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Local product estimates and local-minus-remaining contrasts. Thick bars show 95% intervals. Thin bars show separate four-test intervals for each target. All corrected local intervals include zero. The corrected contrast is below zero only in the later West.
